map.输入展品尺寸与推荐最佳观看视角（或视距系数），计算观众与展品的最佳观看距离及相邻: Input exhibit size and recommended best viewing angle (or viewing-distance factor); compute the best viewing distance for audience and exhibit and reasonable spacing between adjacent exhibits. For exhibition hall layout, avoiding crowding and ensuring viewing experience.
map.展线设计/布展排版时，按展品尺寸与设定视角（水平半角 30°/垂直半角 15°）: In exhibition-line design/layout, infer optimal and minimum viewing distance from exhibit size and set viewing angle (horizontal half-angle 30 deg / vertical half-angle 15 deg), avoiding too close to miss parts or too far to see clearly.
map.单面展墙排布时，按推荐间距估算每米可挂展品数，规划展线长度与展陈密度。: For single-sided display walls, estimate the number of exhibits per meter by recommended spacing, planning the display-line length and density.
map.双人并排观看或大型展品时，增大间距与退后距离，防止相邻展品观看互相干扰、视线遮挡: For two people side by side or large exhibits, increase spacing and viewing distance to prevent mutual interference and sight blocking between adjacent exhibits.
map.观看距离与间距测算示例: Viewing distance and spacing calculation example
map.：某画幅宽 50 cm、高 70 cm、中心高 160 cm、水平半角 30°、: : a piece 50 cm wide, 70 cm high, center height 160 cm, horizontal half-angle 30 deg, vertical half-angle 15 deg, eye height 150 cm, 1 viewer. Horizontal distance = 25 / tan30 deg approx 43.3 cm; vertical distance = (|160-150|+35) / tan15 deg approx 167.9 cm; best viewing distance = max = 167.9 cm; min distance = sqrt(50^2+70^2) x 0.6 approx 51.6 cm; recommended spacing = max(50+60 x 0.8, 50 x 1.5) = 98 cm; about 1 piece per meter.
map.经验值水平最佳视角约 30°（半角）、垂直约 15°；大画幅或需读细节的展品可加: Empirical best viewing angle about 30 deg (half-angle) horizontal, 15 deg vertical; large-format or detail-reading exhibits can enlarge the half-angle (shorter distance), sculptures/3D exhibits should increase viewing distance and spacing. Best distance takes the larger of horizontal and vertical to keep the whole piece within a comfortable angle.
map.推荐间距为何取较大值？: Why take a larger recommended spacing?
map.间距须同时容纳展品宽与观众站位（肩宽×并排人数×0.8 通行余量），且不小于 1: Spacing must accommodate both exhibit width and viewer stance (shoulder width x side-by-side count x 0.8 passage margin), and be no less than 1.5x the piece width, preventing overlap and mutual interference between adjacent exhibits. Larger spacing fits fewer per wall, a trade-off between display density and viewing comfort.
